paper_title: Fully-online Construction of Suffix Trees for Multiple Texts
statement: There are interesting open problems for the left-to-right fully-online suffix tree construction: 1. Is it possible to efficiently maintain complete labels of the edges leading to the leaves? 2. Our bound is amortized, namely, for each new character our algorithm takes O(log σ) amortized time. Is it possible to de-amortize it, e.g. by using techniques in [5, 9, 10]?
context: The main contribution of this paper is an O(N log σ)-time algorithm to maintain the suffix tree for a text collection in the left-to-right fully-online setting, where N and σ are the total text length and the alphabet size, respectively. The key was a non-trivial use of the DAWG. There are interesting open problems for the left-to-right fully-online suffix tree construction: 1. Is it possible to efficiently maintain complete labels of the edges leading to the leaves? 2. Our bound is amortized, namely, for each new character our algorithm takes O(log σ) amortized time. Is it possible to de-amortize it, e.g. by using techniques in [5, 9, 10]?
